transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate you fitting me in. Um, well, I hope I'm explaining this right, and I don't want to waste your time. I'm a chief executive, so I've always got a lot on my plate, and I usually manage everything just fine. 

But... well, for the past year or so, I've been having this little issue. It's probably nothing major, honestly, but I noticed that the smallest things just seem to pull me off what I’m doing before I can stop it. Like, just a phone buzz, or somebody walking past my office door, or... even a random thought about my in-laws popping into my head. It just completely takes my attention away. 

I mean, I'm still keeping the business running, obviously. I'm sure everyone gets a little sidetracked sometimes, right? But it's been bugging me enough that I figured I should ask a professional. Does that... is that the sort of thing people usually come to see you for?
Looking back at your childhood and school years, did you experience similar difficulties with attention or staying focused back then?

Well, um... I guess if I really think about it, yeah, maybe a little? I mean, I wasn't a bad kid or a troublemaker or anything, I promise. I was just... a really enthusiastic kid, I think. 

But looking back, I suppose this sort of thing was around when I was young, too. My teachers, they were always, um, having to move my seat around in class. I guess I talked a bit too much to whoever was sitting next to me. And I'd sometimes get up out of my desk without asking, or I'd just sort of blurt things out before the teacher even finished asking the question. 

I just got so eager, you know? My brain was just moving fast. It wasn't me trying to be disrespectful to them at all. I hope that makes sense... is that the kind of information you were looking for?
Do you find yourself constantly worrying about many different things, and finding it difficult to control that worry?

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, obviously, running a company, there are always things to handle, but I wouldn't say I really *worry* about them constantly. I'm actually a pretty upbeat guy, mostly. 

I don't really get stuck in my head or feel like I can't control my thoughts like that. I usually just try to tackle problems as they come up instead of stressing over them, you know? I hope that's okay to say. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information... is that a normal answer for people to give?
In your day-to-day life now, do you often feel restless inside or find it difficult to sit still for extended periods?

Well, um... I guess I do have a little bit of that sometimes. But I'm definitely not bouncing off the walls or anything, I promise. It's just... well, when I'm really supposed to sit totally still for a long time? Like, um, during nice family dinners, or when I'm at my church volunteer meetings... it just sort of feels like there's this little motor running inside me. 

I just get this urge where I feel like I need to move around, or at least be doing something with my hands, you know? I always try to be really subtle about it, though, so I don't look rude to my family or the committee. I just really like to be productive and keep busy, I guess. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of examples...
